choices.text: Western blot performed on one convalescent sample

explanation.summary: The gold standard is an indirect immunofluorescence assay with R. rickettsii antigen on paired sera showing a fourfold titer rise.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gold standard serologic test is the indirect immunofluorescence assay with Rickettsia rickettsii antigen, performed on two paired serum samples to demonstrate a significant fourfold rise in antibody titers. The first sample should be taken as early as possible, preferably in the first week of symptoms, and the second sample 2 to 4 weeks later. In most cases the first IgG titer is low or negative and the second shows a fourfold increase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A single IgM result is difficult to interpret and IgM is less specific than IgG.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Rickettsia rickettsii is an obligate intracellular organism and cannot be cultured on agar at all.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gram stain is unhelpful for this organism, and culture is not possible on routine media.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Western blot confirmation is part of the Lyme disease pathway, not the rickettsial gold standard.

questions.stem: A physician orders an IgM titer against Rickettsia rickettsii in a patient with a febrile illness after a tick bite. Which of the following is the most important limitation of relying on this test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IgM cross-reacts with Borrelia antigens in essentially all patients

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgM disappears within 48 hours, making the timing nearly impossible

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgM is detectable only if the patient has saved the tick for testing

choices.label: D
choices.text: IgM is less specific than IgG and more likely to be falsely positive

choices.label: E
choices.text: IgM rises weeks after IgG and appears only in severe disease

explanation.summary: IgM antibodies against R. rickettsii are less specific than IgG and more likely to yield false positives, so a concurrent IgG titer should be requested.
explanation.whyCorrect: IgM antibodies usually rise at the same time as IgG near the end of the first week of illness and remain elevated for months or even years. IgM is less specific than IgG and more likely to result in a false positive, so physicians requesting IgM serologic titers should also request a concurrent IgG titer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cross-reactivity in all patients is an overstatement of the specificity problem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IgM can remain elevated for months to years rather than disappearing within days.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serologic testing is performed on patient serum and does not require the tick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgM rises at about the same time as IgG, not weeks later, and is not limited to severe disease.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man in Missouri has fever, severe headache, and a developing rash 6 days after a tick bite. Serologic testing for Rickettsia rickettsii has been sent and is pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin treatment now, because titers rise only weeks into the illness

choices.label: B
choices.text: Withhold therapy until a Gram stain of the rash biopsy is reported

choices.label: C
choices.text: Withhold therapy until blood cultures on routine agar turn positive

choices.label: D
choices.text: Withhold therapy until paired titers show a significant fourfold rise

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold therapy until the tick is recovered and tested for antigen

explanation.summary: Treatment should not be withheld pending serology, because antibody titers only rise weeks after the infection begins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment should not be withheld if Rickettsia rickettsii is suspected, since antibody titers do not rise until weeks after the infection begins. Antibody titers are not useful for the initial diagnosis; they are used to confirm the diagnosis afterward, so for the acutely ill patient the physician must rely on presentation and history.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Rickettsia rickettsii stains poorly with Gram stain, so this result would not guide therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The organism is obligate intracellular and will never grow on routine agar.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting for a fourfold rise means waiting weeks, which delays care in a potentially fatal illness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Although tick tissue can be tested in rare cases, therapy should not depend on recovering the tick.

questions.stem: Ehrlichiosis in the United States is caused by three bacterial species. Which of the following correctly lists them?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and E. muris eauclairensis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and Rickettsia rickettsii

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Rickettsia rickettsii, and Borrelia burgdorferi

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ehrlichia ewingii, Borrelia burgdorferi, and Rickettsia rickettsii

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ehrlichia muris eauclairensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and B. burgdorferi

explanation.summary: Three Ehrlichia species cause ehrlichiosis in the United States: E. chaffeensis, E. ewingii, and E. muris eauclairensis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ehrlichiosis is caused by three bacteria in the United States: Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and Ehrlichia muris eauclairensis. All three are spread by tick bite and produce a similar clinical syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Rickettsia rickettsii is not an Ehrlichia species and does not cause ehrlichiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rickettsia rickettsii causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever and Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease; neither causes ehrlichiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Two of these three organisms cause entirely different tick-borne diseases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Borrelia burgdorferi is the agent of Lyme disease and does not cause ehrlichiosis.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man in Missouri develops fever and headache after a tick bite and is diagnosed with ehrlichiosis. Which two ticks transmit Ehrlichia species in the United States?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amblyomma americanum and Dermacentor variabilis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Amblyomma americanum and Ixodes scapularis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dermacentor andersoni and Rhipicephalus sanguineus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dermacentor variabilis and Dermacentor andersoni

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhipicephalus sanguineus and Ixodes scapularis

explanation.summary: Ehrlichia species are spread by the lone star tick, Amblyomma americanum, and the blacklegged tick, Ixodes scapularis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ehrlichia species are spread through the bite of the lone star tick, Amblyomma americanum, and the blacklegged tick, Ixodes scapularis. Geographically, ehrlichiosis has a distribution similar to Rocky Mountain spotted fever, with most cases in states such as Missouri, Arkansas, and North Carolina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lone star tick is correct, but the American dog tick is a Rocky Mountain spotted fever vector.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These two ticks transmit Rocky Mountain spotted fever, not ehrlichiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both Dermacentor species are vectors of Rickettsia rickettsii rather than Ehrlichia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brown dog tick is a Rocky Mountain spotted fever vector and is not an Ehrlichia vector.

questions.stem: A patient is told that one tick species can transmit both ehrlichiosis and Lyme disease. Which of the following is that shared vector?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amblyomma americanum, the lone star tick

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dermacentor andersoni, the Rocky Mountain wood tick

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dermacentor variabilis, the American dog tick

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ixodes scapularis, the blacklegged tick

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rhipicephalus sanguineus, the brown dog tick

explanation.summary: Ixodes scapularis, the blacklegged tick, transmits both Lyme disease and ehrlichiosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: One of the vectors of Ehrlichia species, Ixodes scapularis, is the same vector that transmits Lyme disease. A single bite from this tick therefore carries the possibility of more than one tick-borne infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lone star tick transmits Ehrlichia species and alpha-gal sensitization, but not Borrelia burgdorferi.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The Rocky Mountain wood tick is a Rocky Mountain spotted fever vector only.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The American dog tick transmits Rickettsia rickettsii and neither of these two diseases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brown dog tick carries Rickettsia rickettsii and does not transmit these two diseases.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and mildly elevated liver enzymes 10 days after a tick bite. A blood smear shows mulberry-shaped clusters of bacteria within vacuoles inside monocytes. These inclusions are called:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Auer rods

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dohle bodies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Howell-Jolly bodies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Morulae

choices.label: E
choices.text: Negri bodies

explanation.summary: Clusters of Ehrlichia inside phagocyte vacuoles form mulberry-shaped aggregates called morulae.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ehrlichia species have a trophism for mononuclear phagocytes such as monocytes and macrophages. Clusters of bacteria inside cell vacuoles may form mulberry-shaped aggregates called morulae, which are highly suggestive of ehrlichiosis when seen on a blood smear.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Auer rods are seen in malignant myeloid cells and are not bacterial clusters.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dohle bodies are cytoplasmic inclusions unrelated to intracellular bacterial aggregates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants within erythrocytes, not bacterial aggregates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Negri bodies are viral inclusions and are not found in monocytes after a tick bite.

questions.stem: Morulae are identified on the blood smear of a patient with a febrile illness after a tick bite. Which of the following best describes the diagnostic role of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms the diagnosis, so no further testing is ever warranted

choices.label: B
choices.text: It excludes ehrlichiosis and points instead to a rickettsial cause

choices.label: C
choices.text: It indicates that the infecting organism is Borrelia burgdorferi

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the only finding that may be used to establish the diagnosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It supports the diagnosis but is not reliable enough to confirm it

explanation.summary: Morulae suggest ehrlichiosis but are not reliable enough to diagnose it; serology is the usual confirmatory test.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clusters of Ehrlichia in cell vacuoles may form morulae, but this finding is not reliable enough to diagnose ehrlichiosis on its own. As with other tick-borne illnesses, serology is a common way to confirm the diagnosis, though treatment should not be withheld pending testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Morulae are not seen in every case and are not considered confirmatory on their own.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Morulae point toward ehrlichiosis rather than away from it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Borrelia burgdorferi is an extracellular spirochete and does not form intracellular morulae.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serology, not the smear, is the common confirmatory test for ehrlichiosis.

questions.stem: Ehrlichia species are small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacteria. Which of the following host cells do they preferentially infect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Circulating erythrocytes and their marrow precursors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hepatocytes located within the periportal zone of the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mononuclear phagocytes such as monocytes and macrophages

choices.label: D
choices.text: Squamous epithelial cells of the skin and oral mucosa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vascular endothelial cells lining small blood vessels

explanation.summary: Ehrlichia species have a trophism for mononuclear phagocytes, that is, monocytes and macrophages.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ehrlichia species are small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacteria with a trophism for mononuclear phagocytes such as monocytes and macrophages. This tropism is why morulae are sought in monocytes on a peripheral blood smear.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ehrlichia species do not parasitize red blood cells or their precursors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatocytes are not the preferred host cell, although liver enzymes may be mildly elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Squamous epithelial cells are not the target of these obligate intracellular bacteria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endothelial cells are the preferred target of Rickettsia rickettsii, which is why that infection causes vasculitis.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman develops fever, headache, malaise, muscle aches, and nausea 9 days after a tick bite in Arkansas and is diagnosed with ehrlichiosis. Which of the following best describes the typical course of this illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Onset 5 to 14 days after the bite, with complications that are rare

choices.label: B
choices.text: Onset after 3 to 4 weeks, with arthritis as the presenting feature

choices.label: C
choices.text: Onset after about 6 months, with a rash present in every single case

choices.label: D
choices.text: Onset within 1 to 2 days, and a presentation unlike other tick illnesses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Onset within hours of the bite, with complications in most patients

explanation.summary: Ehrlichiosis begins 5 to 14 days after the bite with a nonspecific febrile illness, and complications are rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: Onset of ehrlichiosis usually occurs within 5 to 14 days after the tick bite, and the clinical presentation is very similar to early Lyme disease and Rocky Mountain spotted fever, with fever, headache, malaise, muscle ache, and nausea. Complications are rare.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Onset is earlier than 3 to 4 weeks, and arthritis is a late feature of Lyme disease instead.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The incubation period is days to weeks, not months, and rash is not universal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The presentation overlaps considerably with the other tick-borne illnesses rather than being distinctive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Symptoms do not begin within hours, and complications are the exception rather than the rule.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man in Arkansas develops hives, abdominal cramping, and wheezing several hours after eating beef. He has had multiple lone star tick bites over the past year, and this reaction has now happened three times after red meat meals. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allergy to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose, known as alpha-gal syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic ehrlichiosis producing a delayed hypersensitivity response

choices.label: C
choices.text: Late disseminated Lyme disease presenting as gastrointestinal upset

choices.label: D
choices.text: Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome with an allergic component

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rickettsial vasculitis involving mesenteric and cutaneous vessels

explanation.summary: Lone star tick bites can sensitize patients to alpha-gal, producing allergy to mammalian red meat.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lone star ticks do not just transmit ehrlichiosis. Some patients bitten by lone star ticks develop an allergy to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose, or alpha-gal, which is commonly found in the red meat of mammals. Patients who develop this allergy have moderate to severe allergic reactions after red meat consumption, and there is no treatment for alpha-gal syndrome except avoiding red meat.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ehrlichiosis is an acute febrile illness and does not cause recurrent food-triggered allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Late Lyme disease causes arthritis and neurologic and psychiatric symptoms, not food-triggered urticaria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome causes fatigue, pain, and cognitive symptoms rather than food allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rickettsial vasculitis is an acute illness with fever and rash, not a reaction to meals.
